approach: Extend `check_environment_reach` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs; no new `step!` line and no new check. Add a cache-scope trigger with three lexical forms, all read only from behavior criteria (through `scan_segments`), the summary and the workflow deliverables. (D1) A behavior-criterion segment has a cache/artifact word and a CI place: `CI` written exactly (`EnvWord.ci`), workflow(s), runner(s), or the two-word phrase GitHub Actions. (D2) A segment has a CI place, a reuse word (reuse, reused, reuses, reusing) and a result noun (run, runs, pass, passes, result, results, status). This is the early-push shape ('an early push whose CI run is reused at landing') and it fires with no cache word. (D3) A created or modified `.github/workflows/` deliverable exists and a behavior criterion or the summary has a cache/artifact word in a scanned segment. Bare `github` and `actions` are not CI places. When any form fires, one `Environment:` assumption (via `environment_assumptions` and `plain_words`) must hold five parts: a cache/artifact/result noun, a save word, a restore word, a write-rights word and a scope word. If none does, the error names each part missing from the union of the Environment: assumptions. If all parts are present but spread across assumptions, it says to state them in one assumption. The early-return test and the doc comment's 'reads four things' paragraph are updated. The reader rule line in briefs.rs is left unchanged and named as a follow-up in the CHANGELOG item. Tests: new unit tests in reading.rs, new corpus cases plus a declaration test in refusal_corpus.rs, and a CHANGELOG item.

decisions.choice: Extend check_environment_reach; add no new check or step! line.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading says to extend it. Cache save/restore/write scope is a fourth fact of the same Environment: statement. refusing_check, `environment_reach_has_one_step_line` (reading.rs ~5178) and the acceptance doc list stay as they are.

decisions.choice: The trigger has three forms (D1 cache word + CI place, D2 CI place + reuse word + result noun, D3 workflow deliverable + cache word). All read only behavior criteria (through scan_segments) and the summary.
decisions.reason: Finding 1: the er96 wording ('an early push whose CI run is reused at landing') has no cache word, so D1 and D3 alone would miss the class. D2 fires on reuse of a stored CI result, which is the ref-scoped fact that job ignored. The same sentence is used unchanged in the class test and in a corpus refuse case. Reading only behavior criteria and the summary keeps content criteria, the request, assumptions and out_of_scope unread, as the doc comment promises (finding 2). The doc paragraph is reworded to list the new inputs, and fixtures put the cache word in a behavior criterion.

rejected.why: It contradicts the doc comment (surveys.rs:711-712) that a content criterion cannot trigger the check, so repair text could fire it.

rejected.option: Require cache scope for every workflow deliverable
rejected.why: It breaks existing workflow tests (reading.rs ~4840-4856, lint.yml with CI_ENVIRONMENT) and corpus cases environment-ci-workflow-*, and demands cache facts from workflows with no cache.

rejected.why: It refuses in-process caches such as 'the reader caches the survey'.

decisions.choice: CI place = `CI` written exactly, workflow/workflows, runner/runners, or the phrase GitHub Actions. Bare `github`, `actions` and lowercase `ci` are not CI places.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: this follows the existing check, which needs `CI` exact (EnvWord.ci, surveys.rs:417). 'The GitHub API response is cached in memory' and 'the reader caches its actions' stay accepted, and a lowercase `ci` miss is documented as a limit, as the check documents lowercase `pr`.

rejected.option: Reuse ENV_SITE_WORDS as the CI list
rejected.why: It holds github, local, reader, producer and similar words, so a plain product cache would fire.

decisions.choice: Match criteria text through scan_segments and Environment: text through plain_words.
decisions.reason: scan_segments ends a run at a path, identifier or non-command backtick span, so `cache.rs`, `cache_dir` and `lint.yml` trigger nothing. plain_words is what the existing completeness test already uses on assumption text.

rejected.why: It fires on paths, identifiers and words that contain 'cache'.

decisions.choice: The Environment: assumption must hold five parts in one assumption: cache/artifact/result noun, save word, restore word, write-rights word, scope word. The error lists parts missing from the union of Environment: assumptions.
decisions.reason: These are the three questions of the root cause: which ref saves, which runs restore, which may write shared entries. The brief's example sentence satisfies all five. Write-rights words are write, writes, written, writable, readonly, permission, permissions; plain `read` is excluded so a read-only statement does not count as write rights.

rejected.option: Only a cache word and a scope word
rejected.why: A sentence silent on who writes shared entries would pass, which is the gap in both jobs.

The follow-up: reword the line within 220 bytes, for example '...; a CI cache or reused CI result also needs who saves, restores and writes it'.

risks.risk: False positives: a CI place and a cache word in the same behavior criterion with no CI cache involved, or a CI result reuse that is not about a stored result. This would push the refusal share above 3%.
risks.mitigation: CI place needs `CI` written exactly, workflow(s), runner(s) or GitHub Actions. Bare github, actions and lowercase ci are excluded. scan_segments drops paths, identifiers and non-command backticks. The refusal asks for one assumption and the error says what to write. Accept controls cover the in-process cache, a path, the GitHub API response cache and 'CI runs the tests'. The replay at verification measures the real share, and 3% is labelled an estimate that was not measured.

risks.risk: D2 (CI place + reuse word + result noun) is broader than the cache words and may fire on unrelated 'CI ... reuse ... run/result' text, such as the existing 'ci baseline' fixture.
risks.mitigation: That fixture only asserts that check_history_fixture is not the refuser (reading.rs:7500-7506), so it is unaffected. D2 needs all three word kinds in one segment. A control with 'CI runs the tests' and the unchanged own-job test keep it narrow.

risks.risk: A fixture trips an earlier check in refusing_check before check_environment_reach, so `refuser` names another check.
risks.mitigation: Build fixtures from workflow_reading and behavior_reading, which the existing environment tests already pass, and assert check_environment_reach directly as well as refuser. Adjust fixture wording, not the check.

risks.risk: Because the CI-block assumption (CI_ENVIRONMENT) contains 'write' and 'refs', the union of Environment: assumptions would hide a missing write-rights or scope part in a variant test.
risks.mitigation: The variant tests that drop write rights or scope use a CI block with no write word, scope word or cache word, such as 'Environment: the CI job has read access to files on the host', so the union really lacks the part.

risks.risk: The new doc paragraph or CHANGELOG item breaks the old doc/changelog tests, which find their item by the old CAUSE string and assert 8%.
risks.mitigation: Keep the old paragraph and item as they are, and give the new ones a different cause sentence, so the old lookup still finds the old item. Run `cargo test -p athena-core environment_reach` and the corpus test.

risks.risk: The word lists are lexical: a sentence can meet them without being true, or a valid phrasing can miss them.
risks.mitigation: State the limit in the doc comment as the existing check does, and test the brief's example sentence and one variant per missing part. The error tells the reader what to add.

risks.risk: The reader learns the rule only from a refusal, since the rule line in briefs.rs is not updated.
risks.mitigation: The error text states what to write. The CHANGELOG item names the follow-up, and the open question asks the user to decide on it.
